summary: A script is a text file of commands that bash runs in order. Write the steps once, then run them any time with one command.
notes: #!/bin/bash must be the very first line. It tells Linux which program reads the rest of the file.
./report.sh means "report.sh in this folder". bash report.sh also works, and it does not need the execute bit.
Run from music, the script looks for music/cs/roster.txt, which does not exist, so those lines fail. The script keeps going after each error and still prints Report done.
pitfall: Typing report.sh without ./ fails with report.sh: command not found. Bash only looks for commands in the folders listed in PATH, not in the current folder.
